chunks: Ali, from his father, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from one of his companions, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Seek refuge with Allah from the evil ones of your women, and be cautious of the good ones among them, and do not obey them in what is good, lest they invite you to evil.

And he (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Women should not be consulted in secret counsels, nor should they be obeyed regarding close relatives.'
Indeed, when a woman ages, the good of her two halves departs and her evil remains, and that is because her womb becomes barren, her manners become bad, and her tongue becomes sharp.
And indeed, when a man ages, the evil of his two halves departs and his good remains, and that is because his intellect returns to soundness, his opinion becomes firm, and his manners improve.

key_terms.شِرَارِ نِسَائِكُمْ: the evil ones of your women

ai.seo_question: What are the differences between aging in women and men according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), recorded in al-Kafi, highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on prudence in marital dynamics, warning that excessive obedience in righteous matters can become a conduit for sin. It further elaborates on the physiological and psychological changes associated with aging, contrasting the decline in female fertility and character with the maturation of male wisdom and reason. This perspective reflects the classical juristic view of gendered spiritual development within the family structure.
